- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40), as models tend to underreact to bearish sentiment.
- Underestimate late in the horizon when sentiment turns positive (especially > 0.03), as models overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price spikes — model tends to overshoot and then correct, but misses the lagged correction.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive forecast days show upward drift, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to align with historical mean reversion.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate true price — add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to compensate.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate — subtract 0.3–0.8% to correct.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often underestimates true price in the last 7–10 days — apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment for those days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment turns from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the pivot — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days.
